purpose: Shortlist for a bounded native discovery batch, not scoring or a semantic test. No new vision or admissions in this review.

items.locator: Small pale compartment with blue upper rim, left of the central upper figure column

source.quote:
Dense horizontal writing fills areas on both sides. A small pale compartment
with a blue curved upper rim, to the left of the central figures, contains
short lines of writing. That is a visible text enclosure; it does not
determine the text's referent or reading order relative to the larger blocks.

items.source_says: Writing is visibly enclosed in a small compartment.
items.discovery_question: Is the writing enclosed by a genuinely closed drawn boundary, and is the compartment itself attached to another depicted object or merely inserted beside it? This is a concrete nested physical configuration, not a word-owner assignment.
items.inference_not_source: A closed subcontainer could provide a content/container distinction for a later joint reading. Enclosed text need not name the enclosure or its contents.

items.locator: Lower broad arch joining two figure/container vicinities; right continuation to a winding outline and blue terminal with nearby dots

source.quote:
Lower down, a broad arched, partly blue connection joins the vicinity of
two figures in different outlined containers. One has a red band. The right
container continues into a long unpainted winding outline and a blue terminal
form with branching curved strokes and nearby dots. Short inscriptions also
occur beneath the arch and near some drawn extremities.

items.source_says: An arched partly blue connection joins the vicinity of two different containers; one has a red band, and the right continues into another terminal form.
items.discovery_question: Which outlined boundaries are actually continuous across the arch endpoints, and does the terminal have a clearly open edge with marks outside it? Preserve whether the two containers differ in a concrete internal or boundary arrangement.
items.inference_not_source: Continuity plus a marked open termination might distinguish connection/containment relations from mere proximity. No flow, operation, time order or material follows.
items.prior_overlap: GDT790 already used this lower coupled panel and invented inlet/outlet gloss candidates; GDT792 audited host transfer. Do not reuse those labels as physical truth or call the connection newly discovered.

items.locator: Lower rectangular green enclosure, left entering narrow green channel and right small outlet-like form

source.quote:
a green, approximately rectangular enclosure with two horizontal rows of
human figures. Postures, arms and head details vary. The rim has short
transverse marks. No exact figure count or biological identity is assigned.

A narrow green-marked channel meets the enclosure from the left. Further
unpainted outlined connections curve around the lower region, with another
small outletlike form on the right. Contact does not settle flow direction.
A short isolated inscription lies left of the enclosure; these notes do not
attach it to a unique individual figure.

items.source_says: Two figure rows occupy an enclosure; a narrow channel meets it from the left and further outlines curve around the lower region.
items.discovery_question: Does the left channel terminate at the enclosure boundary, cross it, or visibly join a continuous internal filled region? Does the small right form have the same or a different boundary relation?
items.inference_not_source: A visible asymmetric boundary crossing could define a relational contrast. Calling either side inlet/outlet would exceed the notes.
items.prior_overlap: Existing individual-versus-communal enclosure routes are closed; this must not become that broad category contrast or a repeated figure count.

items.locator: Bottom horizontal brown connector and the two red oval terminal bodies

items.source_says: A brown root-like axis extends toward red oval terminal bodies.
items.discovery_question: Are the two red bodies independently outlined objects attached through narrow necks to the same connector, and do their attachment surfaces have a shared unusual feature? Do not reconstruct the complete plant tree.
items.inference_not_source: Could motivate attached-versus-contained or whole-versus-inserted-part alternatives, but the source documents neither removal nor replacement.
items.prior_overlap: Source was just revisited in GDT879; no new geometry or ontology repair should be claimed. Lower priority because it may only reproduce known attached end bodies.

Breite grüne Blätter besitzen teils braune umgeschlagen wirkende Randpartien. Oberhalb der großen roten Wurzel liegen röhrenähnliche Ansätze mit gezeichneten ovalen Endflächen. items.source_says: Tube-like projections have drawn oval end surfaces above the red root-like body.
items.discovery_question: Is there an explicit depicted end surface distinct from an attached continuing stalk, with both states shown together? Count neither tubes nor the complete plant hierarchy.
items.inference_not_source: An end surface can look cut, but this alone proves no removal event or detached matching piece. No such matching piece is documented.
items.prior_overlap: GDT879 already found basal/hierarchy uncertainty here; a repeat aimed only at repairing its graph is excluded. Reserve only for the separate surface-versus-continuation question.

source_vs_inference_rule: Exact quotes are native source reports. All proposed semantic possibilities are explicitly inferences for future observation. None establishes a detached matching part, a removal action, an operational flow or translated word.
selection_limit: These are known visible motifs with specific unresolved local boundary questions; no novelty claim. Excluded generic plant categories, full graph extraction, known f56/f95 links, ring rotation, metadata and same-whole plant matching.
recommended_batch: Start with f75r/f83r/f81v. Preserve actual negatives and unclear connections. Reserve f10r/f13r only if a distinct end-surface question is worth revisiting after their immediate GDT879 exposure; do not spend time repeating plant graph failure.
source_ceiling: Whole-page text can remain the paired text source; no prerequisite of an individually translated branch caption. A local native relation still supplies no linguistic denotation until a concrete competing reading makes a different prediction.
